summary: Deploys are working again: the site rebuilt on 27 Oct and this dashboard now has fresh Google numbers (to 24 Oct). Clicks are up slightly (287, from 255), but the homepage is slipping for the two biggest searches: “osteopath christchurch” fell from 6.2 to 12.1 (#47).

Kaylee's new pregnancy page still doesn't appear in Google's data two weeks after launch (#44). Nothing on the search list shipped this week; the only website changes were careers page updates and moving Kaylee to the top of the homepage practitioners.

topActions.text: Approve #47 and click Ship it. Claude adds “Christchurch” to the homepage's Google title; the homepage fell from 6.2 to 12.1 for “osteopath christchurch”.
In Search Console, request indexing for Kaylee's new pregnancy page and the three retitled condition pages, then resubmit the sitemap (#44, about 5 minutes).
Maddison checks a short plain-English opening for the sports injury page, which is at 6 on Google for “sports injury treatment” but has no clicks (#49).

tldr: Google data (27 Sep – 24 Oct, compared with the 28 days before): 287 clicks (255 before), 181 from people not searching for Meridian by name (150), 34 searches on page 1 (32), 5,240 appearances (4,224). The weekly clicks dipped to 59 in the week of 18 Oct after 84 and 78 the two weeks before. The homepage's average position fell from 9.6 to 15.1. For “osteopath christchurch” it's now 12.1 (6.2 before) and for “acupuncture christchurch” 11.3 (9), so the homepage title (#47) is still the most urgent fix. Good news: the sciatica page climbed again (27.6 → 20.4), headaches improved (22.6 → 15.2), and “fertility acupuncture christchurch” is at 1.8 with 4 clicks. The fertility page's overall average looks worse (62.8) only because it now also appears for unrelated overseas IVF searches.

Still open: Kaylee's pregnancy page (live 15 Oct) has no Google appearances yet (#44). The sports injury page sits at 6.2 for “sports injury treatment” (165 appearances) with no clicks in two months (#49, new). A new search, “maddison aitken nz”, showed Maddison's profile 71 times (#50, new: check whether it's a former name). The ACC page (#25) and fees page (#46) still answer searches that Google's autocomplete keeps suggesting, including the new “how much is acupuncture nz”. #48 is closed because deploys are working again.

Estimated ranks (a US-based web search, not what someone in Christchurch sees): 27 searches checked, including all 8 core ones. For the fourth week, Meridian's own site didn't appear; it showed up only inside directory listings. Added “restore post pregnancy body” and “acupuncture” from Search Console, and “how much is acupuncture nz” and “acupuncture christchurch riccarton” from autocomplete; nothing pruned. Industry news: Google announced no ranking update this week. On 26 Oct it added spam guidance about pages made for sharing, which doesn't affect this site.

Competitors such as Better Health and osteopath-christchurch.com rank with one page per topic, so the gap is now keeping posts coming on topics people already search for. Item #45 suggests the next one.

gaps.title: No off-site citation strategy
gaps.why: Reddit is a major AI-citation source but the platform mix shifted sharply in the Jul-Aug window. UNCHANGED 2026-09-18: no material movement in the Reddit-Perplexity litigation / licensing situation since 31 Jul motion-to-dismiss rejection. Between Jul 1 and Aug 19, 2026, Perplexity supplied 71% of tracked Reddit citations while ChatGPT supplied 23%; ChatGPT Search citations linking to Reddit fell from ~250/day in early Aug to 16/day the week after Aug 14 — a -94% decline in six days. Reddit's Perplexity share is now ~24%, Gemini 0.1%. Item #15 stays on the backlog scoped to Perplexity-visibility only (larger share, smaller more curated source pool means single well-structured posts can surface); skip the ChatGPT-oriented seeding. 90/10 rule still applies: 90% non-promotional, 2–4 weeks of karma-building before any mention of Meridian.

items.title: Add speakable blocks on service intros
items.why: Unlikely to move your rankings. Google has kept this feature in test mode for years, and a large 2026 study found that adding this kind of behind-the-scenes code gave no real lift. It's cheap, but a good one to dismiss.
items.body: Wrap the short answer at the top of each service page in “speakable” code, which marks the text a voice assistant should read aloud. Google has kept speakable in test mode for years, and a 2026 study of 1,885 pages found that adding this kind of behind-the-scenes code made no clear difference to AI or search visibility. The best predictor of being quoted by AI is ranking well in normal Google results. Cheap to do, but low value; a reasonable one to dismiss.

items.title: Auto-fetch Google Business Profile reviews at build time
items.why: Up-to-date review numbers on your own site help visitors trust you, but they don't change your Google ranking by themselves. Getting new Google reviews (#16) is what moves rankings. It also needs a paid Google Places key set up first.
items.body: Pull the Google review count and star rating into the site at build time, so the numbers on the site stay current without manual edits. Needs a Google Places API key (a paid Google Cloud account) set up by the clinic first. Fresh reviews matter a lot for Google Maps rankings, but showing the count on the website doesn't change rankings by itself; getting new reviews (#16) does. Pairs well with #16 once reviews are flowing.

items.title: Answer local Reddit questions to show up in Perplexity AI search
items.why: Reddit mentions mainly help with the Perplexity AI search tool, which few NZ patients use. Time-consuming and hard to measure, so low priority.
items.body: Genuine, helpful answers in NZ Reddit threads (r/chch, r/newzealand) about osteopathy, ACC and back pain, with very occasional mentions of Meridian after weeks of ordinary participation. This mainly helps with Perplexity, an AI search tool few NZ patients use; ChatGPT cites Reddit much less since August. Time-consuming and hard to measure, so low priority.

items.title: Ask happy patients for Google reviews and reply to every review within 48 hours
items.why: Regular new Google reviews, answered within a day or two, are one of the best-proven ways for a local clinic to rank higher in Google Maps results.
items.body: Send a short email after each appointment asking happy patients for a Google review, using the email system the site already has. Reply to every review within a day or two, naming the practitioner or treatment the reviewer mentioned rather than using a template. Recent reviews carry the most weight in Google Maps rankings (Whitespark's 2026 study rates review recency as the top individual local factor), and Google's AI answers also draw on review text. Aim for about one new review a week.

items.title: Build an ACC page: Active Health and Better Health already have one
items.why: Google's autocomplete keeps suggesting “osteopath christchurch acc” and “acupuncture christchurch acc”, and competitors (Better Health, The House of Acupuncture) have ACC pages. Meridian has none. ACC wording is sensitive (see July's rewording), so Nina should check it.
items.body: A single page at /acc/ explaining ACC for patients. Google's autocomplete suggests “is acupuncture covered by acc”, “osteopath christchurch acc” and “acupuncture christchurch acc”, and Search Console shows the sciatica page at 5.7 for “is sciatica covered by acc”. Estimated results for ACC searches show competitors' ACC fees ($18–$25 at three Christchurch acupuncture clinics, $25 at Ara's teaching clinic) but no clinic ACC page. The page should say Meridian is an ACC-registered provider (osteopathy with Nina Hu, acupuncture with Min Jin), what a patient pays, that no referral is needed, and that Meridian isn't part of ACC, with a link to acc.co.nz. Don't describe filing claims on the patient's behalf. Lead with a 40–60 word answer.

items.title: Add a concussion page (only if someone at Meridian treats concussion)
items.why: Check first: none of your practitioners lists concussion as a special interest. Only build this page if someone at Meridian treats concussion and is happy to be named on it. Otherwise, dismiss it.
items.body: A /conditions/concussion/ page built like the existing condition pages. Estimated ranks for “concussion osteopath christchurch”: osteo.co.nz #1, Better Health #2 (through an associate osteopath's profile) and Triskelion Concussion Care #3. Meridian isn't visible, and Search Console shows no concussion searches reaching the site. Post-concussion symptoms (headaches, dizziness, neck pain) overlap with conditions Meridian already treats, but no practitioner lists concussion as a special interest. Confirm someone treats it and is happy to be named before building.

items.title: Check Google's AI Overviews report in Search Console and save a baseline
items.why: Search Console is now connected to this dashboard. The remaining step is a 5-minute look at Google's AI report, so you can later tell whether new pages show up in AI answers.
items.body: Search Console is connected and feeding this dashboard. Its separate AI report (appearances in AI Overviews and AI Mode) isn't pulled in automatically. In Search Console, open Performance, pick the AI features view, set the date range to the last 3 months, and save a screenshot as the “before” picture. The report shows appearances only, not clicks. The 15 Oct title changes and the new pregnancy page are too recent to show there yet, so a screenshot taken now still works as a baseline. No website changes needed.

items.why: Kaylee's pregnancy and postnatal page went live on 15 Oct but still doesn't appear anywhere in Google's data two weeks later. Asking Google to look at it takes about 5 minutes.
items.body: Four pages changed on 15 Oct: the new /services/osteopathy/pregnancy/ page (PR #140) and the back pain, neck pain and headache pages, whose Google titles now include “Christchurch” (#43). The pregnancy page has no Search Console appearances yet. In Search Console, paste each address into the search bar at the top (URL inspection) and click “Request indexing”, then open Sitemaps and resubmit /sitemap.xml. Check the Pages report in two weeks to confirm the new page is indexed. No website changes needed.

items.why: The sciatica page climbed again, from 27.6 to 20.4, and is at 4–6 for “sciatica treatment christchurch” and “is sciatica covered by acc”. A practical article gives Google a second, linked page on the topic.
items.body: A short post answering what people already search for: “sciatica treatment” (Search Console 12.7), “sciatica specialist” (15.3), “can an osteopath help with sciatica” (8.2), “is sciatica covered by acc” (5.7) and “sciatica treatment pregnancy” (Google autocomplete). Jonathan lists sciatica as a special interest, so he should check the clinical content. The pregnancy acupuncture post sits at 8 with 132 appearances but no clicks yet, so this stays experimental.

items.body: A short /fees/ page listing the consultation fees already in site.js (ACC $80–$85, private $115–$120) and which services they cover, with a heading like “Osteopathy & acupuncture fees in Christchurch”. Estimated results for price searches show directories and pages quoting a price: Ara's teaching clinic ($50, or $25 with ACC) and a Fresha average of $60 for Christchurch acupuncture. Google's autocomplete now also suggests “how much is acupuncture nz”. Add a one-line ACC note that links to the ACC page (#25) once it exists. Link it from the footer and the booking page. Nina should confirm the prices are current before it goes live. No clinical claims.

items.body: The homepage's Google title is “Osteopathy, Acupuncture, Dry Needling & Herbal Medicine — Meridian Osteopathy”, with no place name. It is the page Google shows for “acupuncture christchurch” (318 appearances, 2 clicks) and “osteopath christchurch” (130 appearances, 4 clicks), both now off the first page; the homepage's average position fell from 9.6 to 15.1. The main heading already says Christchurch. After the same change, the sciatica page moved from 27.6 to 20.4. Wording only, no clinical changes.

items.body: The page already has a Christchurch title (#40) and ranks on page 1 for “sports injury treatment” (6.2), “sports injury treatments” (7.6) and “running injury prevention christchurch” (13.1), with 239 appearances and 0 clicks. Many of these searchers want to know what to do right now. Open the page with a short plain answer: what to do in the first few days, when to get it looked at, and what a first visit includes; then reword the Google description to match. Maddison lists sport as a clinical interest, so she should check the advice. Experimental: Google's numbers show the ranking, not why people don't click.

items.why: Google showed Maddison's profile 71 times for “maddison aitken nz” this month (position 5.3), with no clicks. If that's a former name, saying so on her profile would help people find her.
items.body: Search Console shows a new search, “maddison aitken nz”, leading to Maddison Moffat's profile 71 times in 28 days, at position 5.3 with no clicks. Ask Maddison whether she has practised or registered as Maddison Aitken. If she has and is happy for it to be shown, Claude can add “formerly Maddison Aitken” to her profile and add the name to the brand list in auditConfig. If it's someone else, dismiss this item.
